C. Areas of Joint Coordination
In addition to the land and water areas made available to the United States under the proposed Treaty for the administration, operation and maintenance of the Canal and for its protection and defense, the Treaty also provides for joint U.S.-Panamanian regimes for the management of a number of other land and water areas. These arrangements are designed to give the U.S. the ability to ensure that future actions provide adequate environmental protection.
The areas for joint coordination fall into three major categories:
1. Sixteen Area of Military Coordination (including seven military housing areas) will be under U.S. Control, but avilable for use by Panamanian forces. U.S. fire prevention, safety and sanitation standards will apply in these areas. There will be joint U.S.-Panamanian military police patrols for these areas and it is anticipated that this will result in even more effective control of trespassers, wood cutters and unauthorized hunters than is presently the case. This should result in enhanced protection to the Fort Sherman  Achiote Road area, for example.
2. A Joint Committee on Ports will coordinate activities of the Ports of Balboa and Cristobal and the operation of the Panama Railroad, which will revert to Panama under the Treaty. Under the Treaty's terms, Panama must maintain its port installations and the railroad in efficient operating condition and may not change the use of or dispose of facilities without U.S. approval. Safety, fire and oil pollution standards must be maintained at the level of current U.S. standards. Implementation planning is still under way, but these provisions appear adequate to ensure proper environmental safeguards. No significant construction activity is planned.
